papers.title: Molecular Evaluation of Deep Eutectic Solvents for Wet Algae Lipid Extraction and Biofuel Production.
papers.abstract: Microalgae represent promising feedstocks for biofuel production, yet cell-wall disruption remains a critical bottleneck for scaling up lipid extraction. This study evaluates four cholinium-based ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) as green, energy-efficient pretreatment agents to facilitate the lipid release from Chlorella vulgaris under wet conditions. A geranic acid-based DES (CG 1-2 DES) was identified as the optimal agent, demonstrating direct wet biomass extraction with substantial process energy savings at comparable overall lipid yields. To minimize the energetic cost
papers.summary: This study evaluates cholinium-based ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents as green pretreatment agents for extracting lipids from wet Chlorella vulgaris biomass, addressing the cell-wall disruption bottleneck in algal biofuel production. A geranic acid-based DES (CG 1-2 DES) was identified as optimal, enabling direct wet biomass extraction with substantial energy savings at comparable lipid yields.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Natural BACE1 Inhibitors with Enzymatic and Cellular Validation.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by excessive accumulation of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides in the brain. Beta-secretase 1 (BACE1), the rate-limiting enzyme in the amyloidogenic processing pathway of amyloid precursor protein (APP), has been widely recognized as an important therapeutic target for reducing Aβ production. In the present study, nine machine learning-based predictive models for BACE1 inhibitors were constructed using Naïve Bayes (NB) and Recursive Partitioning (RP) algorithms. Subsequently, internal and external validations were conducte
papers.summary: This study built nine machine learning models (using Naïve Bayes and Recursive Partitioning) to predict BACE1 inhibitors, a key enzyme target in Alzheimer's disease. The models were validated internally and externally, and top predicted natural compounds were confirmed through enzymatic and cellular assays. This demonstrates a practical ML-guided pipeline for discovering natural-product BACE1 inhibitors.

papers.title: Conformation- and Compound-Dependence of Ribose/2'-Deoxyribose Retention Patterns in Pyrimidine-Nucleoside Phosphorylase from Bacillus subtilis: A Four-Structure Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: In pyrimidine-nucleoside phosphorylase (PyNP), how the conformational state shapes substrate recognition remains poorly understood. In this study, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) with MM-PB-(GB)-SA decomposition was performed on four structures of PyNP from Bacillus subtilis spanning the conformational range: the open 5OLN, the semi-open 5EP8orig, an energy-minimized contracted (closed-like) model 5EP8 min, and the cross-species closed-state crystal 1BRW, the last added to define the closed-state end. Thirteen structural probes were used (ten purine-like ribose/2'-deoxyribose analogues and th
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations and MM-PB(GB)SA binding free energy decomposition to compare four conformational states of Bacillus subtilis pyrimidine-nucleoside phosphorylase, probing how open versus closed conformations affect recognition of ribose and 2'-deoxyribose nucleoside analogues. The results reveal that sugar retention patterns depend on both the enzyme's conformational state and the specific compound, providing mechanistic insight into substrate discrimination in this phosphorylase.

papers.title: Multiobjective Fluorescent Molecule Design with a Data-Physics Dual-Driven Generative Framework.
papers.abstract: Designing fluorescent small molecules requires simultaneous control over optical responses, brightness, and physicochemical constraints across vast, underexplored chemical spaces. Conventional generate-score-screen approaches become impractical under such realistic design specifications, owing to their low search efficiency, unreliable generalizability of machine-learning predictions, and the prohibitive cost of quantum chemical calculations. Here, we present LUMOS, a data- and physics-driven framework for inverse design of fluorescent molecules. LUMOS couples the generator and predictor withi
papers.summary: LUMOS is a generative framework for inverse design of fluorescent small molecules that combines data-driven machine learning with physics-based quantum chemical calculations. It addresses the inefficiency of traditional generate-score-screen approaches by jointly optimizing multiple objectives like optical response, brightness, and physicochemical properties. The method enables efficient exploration of vast chemical spaces for fluorescent molecule discovery.

papers.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Oxidation Resistance for Tertiary Phosphines Using Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potential-Aided Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Tertiary phosphines play important roles in a wide range of chemical reactions, but they suffer from oxidation in air. Here, we propose a computational workflow for the comprehensive prediction of oxidation resistance in tertiary phosphines based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using Matlantis PFP, a universal machine learning interatomic potential (uMLIP). MD simulations were conducted for 51 different tertiary phosphines and analyzed to estimate mean survival time by survival analysis (τ). The resulting τ reproduced experimentally and theoretically recognized trends in oxidation resis
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational workflow that uses a universal machine learning interatomic potential (Matlantis PFP) to run molecular dynamics simulations on 51 tertiary phosphines and predict their oxidation resistance via survival analysis. The predicted mean survival times reproduce known experimental and theoretical trends, offering a fast screening approach for air-stable phosphine ligand design.

papers.title: Bridging Visual Intuition and Chemical Expertise: A Virtual Collaborative Framework for Autonomous Nonadiabatic Dynamics Analysis.
papers.abstract: Analyzing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics trajectories traditionally heavily relies on expert intuition and visual pattern recognition, a process that is difficult to formalize. We present VisU, a vision-driven framework that leverages the complementary strengths of two state-of-the-art large language models (Doubao-Seed-1.6-Vision and DeepSeek-V3.2) to establish a "virtual research cooperation". This operates through a "Mentor-Engineer-Student" paradigm that mimics the collaborative intelligence of a professional chemistry laboratory. Within this ecosystem, the Mentor provides physical intuit
papers.summary: The authors present VisU, a vision-driven framework that combines two large language models (Doubao-Seed-1.6-Vision and DeepSeek-V3.2) in a 'Mentor-Engineer-Student' paradigm to autonomously analyze nonadiabatic molecular dynamics trajectories. The system mimics the collaborative intelligence of a chemistry lab, using visual pattern recognition and chemical expertise to interpret complex simulation data that traditionally requires expert intuition.

papers.title: Conformational Preference Classification of Integrin-Binding Ligands Using Free Energy Perturbation.
papers.abstract: Integrins are crucial cell adhesion receptors and attractive therapeutic targets, but developing safe small-molecule inhibitors has been challenging, at least in part due to inadvertent partial agonism caused by stabilization of the integrin's open, high-affinity state. To address this challenge, we present a computational approach using Absolute Binding Free Energy Perturbation (AB-FEP) calculations to predict whether a ligand will stabilize the open or closed integrin states, leveraging the difference between the ligand's binding free energy to the respective end states. Despite challenges p
papers.summary: This study presents a computational method using Absolute Binding Free Energy Perturbation (AB-FEP) to predict whether small-molecule ligands will stabilize the open (active) or closed (inactive) conformation of integrins. By comparing binding free energies to each end state, the approach aims to help design safer integrin inhibitors that avoid unintended partial agonism. The work addresses a key challenge in developing integrin-targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: Enhanced Sampling of Protein Conformations in AlphaFold3 with Repulsive Bias in the Diffusion Generative Model.
papers.abstract: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3 (AF3), to predict. It has been observed that AF3 sometimes fails to capture ligand-induced conformational changes, even though it explicitly includes ligand molecules that induce such changes. To address this challenge, we develop an enhanced sampling scheme that leverages the diffusion-based generative model used in AF3 to predict protein structures. Interpreting the diffusion generative model as a stochastic sampling process analogous to molec
papers.summary: The authors introduce an enhanced sampling method that adds a repulsive bias to AlphaFold3's diffusion-based generative model, allowing it to explore alternative protein conformations rather than collapsing to a single predicted structure. This approach helps capture ligand-induced conformational changes that standard AF3 often misses, improving the diversity of predicted structural ensembles.

papers.title: Site-specific phosphorylation of Ser352 drives aggregation of Tau R4 under acidosis conditions.
papers.abstract: In Alzheimer's disease, neurons undergo acidosis as their pH drops from ∼7.1 to ∼6.5. Here we elucidate the molecular mechanism of specific Tau aggregation only at this lower pH. We show that a specific phosphorylation event in the Tau R4 domain is coupled to this pH drop to drive a defined phase transition from condensates to fibrils. Using a combination of experimental and computational studies, our results demonstrate that site-specific phosphorylation of Ser352 is the molecular switch that induces aggregation of Tau only at the more acidic, disease-related pH. We designed and synthesized a
papers.summary: This study identifies phosphorylation of Ser352 in the Tau R4 domain as a molecular switch that triggers Tau aggregation specifically under the acidic conditions (pH ~6.5) found in Alzheimer's disease neurons. Combining experimental and computational approaches, the authors show this site-specific modification drives a phase transition from liquid condensates to fibrils only at disease-relevant pH. The work provides a mechanistic link between neuronal acidosis and Tau pathology.

papers.title: Protein eXplosion Imaging (PXI): Protein Structures from Laser-Driven Explosions.
papers.abstract: We investigate the structural information retained in the distribution of explosion ion trajectories from proteins subjected to strong ionization. Using molecular-dynamics simulations and machine-learning analysis benchmarked against an analytical approach, we show that low-resolution structural information can be retrieved from the explosion distributions alone. An ensemble of convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps recovers the radius of gyration and the three semi-axes of an ellipsoidal molecular envelope with prediction errors of 1.2 Å and 1.5 Å, respectively,
papers.summary: This paper explores whether structural information about proteins can be recovered from the ion trajectories produced when proteins are exploded by intense laser ionization. Using molecular dynamics simulations and convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps, the authors show that low-resolution features like radius of gyration and ellipsoidal envelope axes can be predicted with errors around 1.2–1.5 Å. The work suggests a proof-of-concept route to protein shape determination from explosion imaging data.

papers.title: Simulating Infrared Spectra of Matrix Isolation Experiments: What Works Best?
papers.abstract: Matrix isolation is an experimental technique which allows spectroscopists to observe highly reactive or weakly bound systems by trapping them in frozen noble gas matrices. In this work, we studied the viability of using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to simulate several H2S·amine complexes isolated in solid argon crystals, comparing the results with conventional density functional theory (DFT) harmonic and anharmonic calculations to assess the most practical and accurate method to calculate the vibrational spectrum of such systems. While AIMD accurately predicted the intensity ratios of
papers.summary: This study compares ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) against conventional DFT harmonic and anharmonic calculations for simulating infrared spectra of H2S·amine complexes trapped in solid argon matrices. AIMD accurately predicted intensity ratios, suggesting it is a viable approach for modeling matrix isolation experiments, though trade-offs in computational cost and accuracy are discussed.

papers.title: Ophiopogonin D suppresses non-small cell lung cancer progression by targeting exosomal MALAT1 to enhance dendritic cell maturation.
papers.abstract: Tumor-immune cell crosstalk critically shapes the progression of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the mechanisms underlying exosome-mediated immune suppression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized exosomal lncRNA-mediated immunoregulatory axis targeted by the natural compound Ophiopogonin D (OP-D). Transcriptomic profiling and mechanistic rescue experiments revealed that Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC)-derived exosomal MALAT1 suppresses dendritic cell (DC) maturation by increasing SIRT1 expression and attenuating p65 phosphorylation. Computational model
papers.summary: This study identifies a new immune-evasion mechanism in non-small cell lung cancer, where exosomes carrying the lncRNA MALAT1 suppress dendritic cell maturation by boosting SIRT1 and reducing p65 phosphorylation. The natural compound Ophiopogonin D blocks this axis, restoring dendritic cell maturation and slowing tumor progression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Comprehensive insights into thermodynamic stability, optoelectronic properties, thermoelectric properties, and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution potential of halide double perovskites Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, I): first-principles and AIMD approach.
papers.abstract: Rubidium (Rb)-based halide double perovskites (HDPs) possessing tunable optoelectronic features have emerged as promising substances for optoelectronic, thermoelectric, and photocatalytic hydrogen production technologies. In the present work, Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, and I) HDPs are reported using a first-principles approach. The optimized lattice parameters, tolerance factors, and formation energy validate the cubic phase and thermal integrity of the studied HDPs at 300 K. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulation confirms thermal stability at 300 K, and phonon spectra validate dynamic sta
papers.summary: This study uses first-principles calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics to characterize the halide double perovskites Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, I), confirming their cubic phase, thermal and dynamic stability, and tunable optoelectronic, thermoelectric, and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution properties. The work suggests these materials are promising candidates for sustainable energy applications such as thermoelectrics and photocatalytic water splitting.

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Computational Framework for Anti-Persister Tuberculosis Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Latent tuberculosis (TB), caused by dormant, non-replicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), afflicts an estimated 1.7 billion individuals globally and remains a principal barrier to TB eradication. Dormant bacilli are phenotypically tolerant to conventional antibiotics and survive through continued dependence on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and the electron transport chain (ETC), making bioenergetic enzymes, including the F1Fo-ATP synthase, cytochrome bcc:aa3 supercomplex, Type II NADH dehydrogenase (NDH-2) and cytochrome bd oxidase, compelling drug targets. This review proposes and r
papers.summary: This review proposes a multi-scale computational framework for discovering drugs that target dormant, drug-tolerant Mycobacterium tuberculosis persisters, which cause latent TB in roughly 1.7 billion people. It highlights bioenergetic enzymes of oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain—such as F1Fo-ATP synthase, the cytochrome bcc:aa3 supercomplex, NDH-2, and cytochrome bd oxidase—as promising targets for new anti-persister therapies.

papers.title: Unraveling insights for ion transport enhancement by metal-organic framework-5 in polyethylene oxide and polyvinylidene fluoride electrolytes: classical molecular dynamics and metadynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The structural and dynamical properties of simulation systems consisting of metal organic frameworks (MOFs), particularly MOF-5, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) salt, and two well-known polymers, poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO), in different compositions were investigated using classical molecular dynamics (cMD) and well-tempered metadynamics (WT-MD) simulations. The cMD simulations revealed that the PEO-based hybrid electrolyte system containing LiTFSI salt and MOF-5 (System D) exhibits the highest diffusion coefficient for Li+ ions and comp
papers.summary: This study uses classical molecular dynamics and well-tempered metadynamics simulations to investigate how MOF-5 affects lithium ion transport in polymer electrolytes based on PEO and PVDF with LiTFSI salt. The PEO-based hybrid system containing MOF-5 showed the highest Li+ diffusion coefficient, suggesting MOF-5 can enhance ion transport in solid polymer electrolytes.

papers.title: tris-Schiff Base Derivatives Containing Flurbiprofen as Potential Tyrosinase Inhibitors: Synthesis, In Vitro Evaluation, Molecular Docking, DFT and Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: A novel series of tris-Schiff bases of flurbiprofen has been synthesised via multi-step reactions, structures were deduced by means of HR-ESI-MS, 13C- and 1H-NMR spectroscopy and screened for their in vitro tyrosinase inhibitory potential. All the synthetic derivatives attributed noteworthy inhibition except compounds (11, 14 and 16), while eight compounds (5, 6, 7, 8, 19, 24, 22 and 18) were found potent comparing them with the standard kojic acid. Furthermore, the remaining nine compounds showed good to less inhibitory activity. A para-nitro containing compound 5 attributed the powerful tyro
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of tris-Schiff base derivatives of flurbiprofen and tested their ability to inhibit tyrosinase, an enzyme relevant to melanin production and browning. Several compounds showed stronger inhibition than the standard kojic acid, with compound 5 (bearing a para-nitro group) being the most potent. Molecular docking, DFT, and dynamics simulations were used to rationalize the binding and activity of these compounds.

papers.title: Discovery and molecular insights of a novel pea-derived antioxidant peptide: From quantum chemical insights to oxidative stability of walnut oil.
papers.abstract: This study identified novel antioxidant peptides from defeasated pea protein and characterized their molecular properties and protective effects in a lipid system. Following ultrafiltration, Sephadex G-15 purification, Nano LC-MS/MS identification, and in silico screening, five unreported peptides (F1-F5) were selected for evaluation. Antioxidant activities varied across DPPH, ABTS, and hydroxyl radical assays, reflecting sequence- and assay-specific differences. Integrated experimental and computational analyses identified GIPYWTY (F1) as the lead peptide. Molecular docking revealed favorable
papers.summary: This study identified five novel antioxidant peptides from pea protein, with GIPYWTY (F1) emerging as the lead candidate based on combined experimental and computational screening. The peptide showed protective effects against oxidation in walnut oil, suggesting potential as a natural food preservative.

papers.title: Fast and accurate construction of multiple sequence alignments from protein language embeddings with ARIES.
papers.abstract: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) is a foundational task in computational biology, underpinning protein structure prediction, evolutionary analysis, and domain annotation. Traditional MSA algorithms rely on pairwise amino acid substitution matrices derived from conserved protein families. While effective for aligning closely related sequences, these scoring schemes struggle in the low-identity "twilight zone". Here, we present a new approach for constructing MSAs leveraging amino acid embeddings generated by protein language models (PLMs), which capture rich evolutionary and contextual informa
papers.summary: ARIES is a new method that builds multiple sequence alignments by using embeddings from protein language models instead of traditional amino acid substitution matrices. This approach improves alignment accuracy, particularly for distantly related proteins in the low-identity 'twilight zone' where conventional methods struggle. The method is also computationally fast, making it practical for large-scale use.

papers.title: Discovery of dietary polyphenols targeting the autoinducer-2 quorum sensing system of pathogenic bacteria.
papers.abstract: Targeting autoinducer-2 (AI-2) quorum sensing (QS) systems with dietary compounds represents a promising strategy to combat pathogens, yet mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we develop a machine learning-driven framework combining computational screening with multi-level experimental analysis to identify AI-2 quorum sensing interference molecules (QSIMs). A graph neural network (GNN)-based classifier (AI2IMpred) screens over 7000 phytochemicals and identifies dietary polyphenols as potent QSIMs. Using Salmonella Typhimurium LT2 as a model, we demonstrate that 17 polyphenols, including pterostilb
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning framework (AI2IMpred, a graph neural network classifier) to screen over 7,000 phytochemicals for molecules that interfere with the autoinducer-2 (AI-2) quorum sensing system of pathogenic bacteria. Dietary polyphenols were identified as potent quorum sensing interference molecules, with 17 polyphenols validated experimentally using Salmonella Typhimurium LT2 as a model organism.

papers.title: Structure-guided discovery of novel ERα-binding peptides with in vitro antiproliferative activity.
papers.abstract: Uterine leiomyoma (UL) is an oestrogen-dependent tumour, and ERα is closely associated with abnormal proliferation of UL cells. This study used structure-guided virtual screening of a 59,319-member peptide library, followed by molecular docking, MST, MD simulation, MM/PBSA analysis, MTT assays, ERα knockdown, and RT-qPCR, to identify ERα-binding peptides. Four peptides showed ERα binding, among which Peptide-4 exhibited the lowest Kd value (9.3 ± 0.5 nM). Docking, MD simulation, and MM/PBSA analyses suggested a relatively stable ERα-Peptide-4 binding mode supported by hydrogen-bonding, hydroph
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study used structure-guided virtual screening of a large peptide library to identify novel peptides that bind ERα, the estrogen receptor implicated in uterine leiomyoma proliferation. Peptide-4 showed the strongest binding (Kd ~9.3 nM) and demonstrated antiproliferative activity in vitro, with binding validated by molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and binding free energy analysis. The work provides a starting point for developing peptide-based ERα inhibitors for estrogen-dependent tumors.

papers.title: Identification of new fucosyltransferase-8 inhibitors: An integrated biochemical, biophysical, and computational approach.
papers.abstract: The α-1,6-fucosyltransferase (FUT8) mediated core fucosylation is responsible for several pathophysiological processes, including prostate cancer progression. FUT8 is a promising therapeutic target owing to its effects on cell migration and its capacity to convert androgen-dependent prostate cancer cells into androgen-independent cells. This study, therefore, investigates potential FUT8 inhibitors as therapeutic options for prostate cancer by targeting FUT8-mediated core fucosylation using in vitro, biophysical, and computational approaches. Eight of the 265 compounds showed significant cytoto
papers.summary: This study screened 265 compounds and identified eight that inhibit FUT8, an enzyme responsible for core fucosylation that drives prostate cancer progression and androgen independence. The inhibitors were validated using biochemical, biophysical, and computational methods, suggesting FUT8 as a druggable target for prostate cancer therapy.

papers.title: Network toxicology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for bisphenol A neurotoxicity in depression pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA), a widespread environmental endocrine disruptor, can cross the blood-brain barrier and exert neurotoxic effects closely associated with depression pathogenesis. However, the precise molecular targets and signaling pathways mediating BPA-induced depression remain poorly understood. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, GEO transcriptomic dataset analysis, and in vivo experimental validation in mice to systematically investigate the potential toxicological targets and underlying mechanisms of BPA in depression. BPA-related t
papers.summary: This study combines network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and mouse experiments to identify molecular targets and pathways through which the environmental pollutant bisphenol A (BPA) may contribute to depression. The authors integrate transcriptomic data with computational predictions and in vivo validation to propose mechanistic links between BPA neurotoxicity and depression pathogenesis.

papers.title: Experimental Study on Anxiolytic and Antidepressant Effects of Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules in CUMS Mice and Prediction of Underlying Molecular Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the in‑vivo pharmacological effects of Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules(ZCK) on CUMS‑induced anxiety‑ and depression‑like behaviors in mice. Post‑hoc exploratory analyses including network pharmacology and molecular docking were further performed to generate potential mechanistic hypotheses for its anti‑depressant action.
papers.summary: This study tested Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules (ZCK) in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model, finding that the treatment reduced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. Follow-up network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were used to generate hypotheses about the molecular targets and pathways underlying these effects. The work is exploratory and primarily hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Antidepressant Mechanisms and Side Effects: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Study of Amitriptyline, Mirtazapine, and Escitalopram for Treating Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.abstract: Amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and escitalopram are effective antidepressants for treating major depressive disorder (MDD). Our study aimed to use computational biology to understand the mechanisms for the similarities and differences in efficacies and side effects of these drugs.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular docking to compare how three antidepressants (amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and escitalopram) work at the molecular level and why they differ in efficacy and side effects. The computational approach identifies shared and distinct protein targets, offering mechanistic explanations for their clinical profiles in treating major depressive disorder.

papers.title: Monomeric CRP is prevalent in the blood of patients with rheumatoid arthritis and correlates with clinically relevant markers.
papers.abstract: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) is a hallmark of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares. CRP exists as pentameric (pCRP) and monomeric (mCRP) isoforms with distinct functions, with pCRP generally pro-inflammatory and mCRP more immunomodulatory. Standard clinical assays do not distinguish between these forms, and it remains unclear whether elevated CRP in RA reflects structural variation. We investigated CRP isoform distribution and function in RA using biomolecular and biophysical approaches.
papers.summary: This study shows that monomeric CRP (mCRP), a less inflammatory isoform of the standard CRP biomarker, is prevalent in the blood of rheumatoid arthritis patients and correlates with clinically relevant disease markers. Since standard clinical assays cannot distinguish between pentameric and monomeric CRP, this finding suggests current CRP measurements may be missing important structural information about disease activity.

papers.title: Integrating network analysis and machine learning to explore the pharmacological targets and associations of oleanolic acid in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a major type of non-small cell lung cancer, has high incidence and mortality rates. Oleanolic acid (OA), a natural pentacyclic triterpene compound, has demonstrated potential anti-tumor effects but its pharmacological effects in LUAD remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study combines network analysis and machine learning to identify potential pharmacological targets of oleanolic acid, a natural triterpene compound, in lung adenocarcinoma. The authors aim to clarify how oleanolic acid might exert anti-tumor effects in this common type of lung cancer.

papers.title: Global research trends in tuberculosis drug-resistance mechanisms: a bibliometric and cross-database analysis.
papers.abstract: Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) remains a major challenge to global tuberculosis control. In 2024, approximately 390,000 individuals developed multidrug- or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) worldwide, while treatment coverage remained limited to 42%, highlighting persistent gaps in DR-TB management. The mechanisms underlying DR-TB involve resistance-associated mutations, bacterial adaptation, host-pathogen interactions, and drug-target-related processes. A comprehensive evaluation of research trends is needed to clarify the evolution and future directions of this field.
papers.summary: This bibliometric and cross-database analysis maps global research trends on tuberculosis drug-resistance mechanisms, covering topics such as resistance-associated mutations, bacterial adaptation, host-pathogen interactions, and drug-target processes. It highlights persistent gaps in DR-TB management, noting that only 42% of the estimated 390,000 MDR/RR-TB cases in 2024 received treatment. The study aims to clarify the evolution of the field and identify future research directions.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis prioritizes ALDH2 as a candidate Puerarin-associated target linked to macrophage infiltration in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Puerarin is a bioactive isoflavone with reported anti-tumor and immunomodulatory activities; however, its candidate molecular targets and associations with the immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD) remain incompletely defined. This study integrated computational analyses with a murine LUAD model to prioritize candidate puerarin-associated targets and evaluate their relationships with immune-cell changes.
papers.summary: This study used integrative multi-omics and computational analyses, combined with a mouse lung adenocarcinoma model, to identify ALDH2 as a candidate molecular target associated with puerarin treatment. The findings suggest ALDH2 may link puerarin's anti-tumor effects to macrophage infiltration in the tumor immune microenvironment. The work provides a prioritized target hypothesis but relies largely on computational prediction and preliminary murine validation.

papers.title: Identification of natural TLR4 modulators through network pharmacology and molecular modeling in SARS-CoV-2 Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection.
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii exacerbates hyperinflammation via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated immune pathways. Using network pharmacology, an integrated protein-protein interaction network identified 30 key inter-species hubs comprising viral, bacterial, and human host proteins, with TLR4 achieving a high MCC score (722), highlighting its high topological centrality as a host immune target. Virtual screen of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex identified three top candidates, CID5898023, CID5403474, and CID74977829, with docki
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify TLR4 as a central host immune hub in SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection, then virtually screens 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex. Three top candidate compounds (CID5898023, CID5403474, CID74977829) were identified through molecular docking as potential natural modulators of TLR4-driven hyperinflammation.

papers.title: HIST1H2BJ is associated with poor prognosis and an immune-altered tumor microenvironment in glioma.
papers.abstract: Glioma, the most prevalent and aggressive primary malignant brain tumor, is associated with poor clinical outcomes. There is an urgent need for novel biomarkers to predict survival and therapeutic response, as existing markers offer limited prognostic utility.
papers.summary: This study identifies HIST1H2BJ, a histone gene, as a prognostic biomarker in glioma, linking its expression to poor survival outcomes. The authors also report that HIST1H2BJ is associated with an immune-altered tumor microenvironment, suggesting it may influence immune evasion or response. These findings point to HIST1H2BJ as a potential target for risk stratification and immunotherapy strategies in glioma.
